negative_results.proposition_refuted: ClayCode semantic identity can safely canonicalize all collection-like sequences as unordered/deduplicated values.
negative_results.result: In 20,000/20,000 tested ordered-operation swaps, execution changed. The deliberately over-normalizing canonicalizer nevertheless produced the same semantic hash in 20,000/20,000 cases.
negative_results.implication: Canonicalization must be driven by static collection semantics. Ordered sequences remain order-sensitive; set-like fields may sort/deduplicate; contract/provenance identity remains separate.
negative_results.falsifier_or_scope_limit: This bounded micro-language experiment does not prove all future ClayCode collection semantics; nested/maps/weighted/multiset forms need their own typed rules and fuzz fixtures.

negative_results.proposition_refuted: The current G9 V3 source and current grammar.ebnf are already a self-consistent executable surface pair.
negative_results.result: Current source uses relational >/<, a POS|NEG field type, a digit-leading 4B_emits identifier and an if statement that the current grammar does not admit.
negative_results.implication: BASE cannot freeze parser/canonicalizer behavior from these two artifacts without first reconciling the surface contract or locating a newer authoritative grammar/parser.
negative_results.falsifier_or_scope_limit: A newer authoritative parser/grammar may exist outside the inspected admitted stack; locating and successfully roundtripping G9 V3 would supersede this artifact-level negative result.
